title: 1.14.0 and 1.14.1 ship known bugs — install 1.14.2 or newer

detection.reason: the add-on version is resolved to a MINOR from the controller image tag, so no rule can compare patch levels

quote: The following bugs were found in `v1.14.1` and have been fixed in `v1.14.2`:
remediation: Pin at least v1.14.2: 1.14.0 shipped the wrong cainjector image and 1.14.1 copied the CSR's critical flag instead of recalculating it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.image | test("cert-manager")) | .image'  # any 1.14.0 or 1.14.1 tag here is one of the two buggy patches

title: The startupapicheck job pulls a new image, which a restricted registry may not have

detection.reason: the startupapicheck Job exists only during a Helm install/upgrade, so it is not in a steady-state inventory; whether YOUR registry mirrors the new image is not a cluster fact at all

quote: The startupapicheck job uses a new OCI image called startupapicheck, instead of the ctl image. If you run in an environment in which images cannot be pulled, be sure to include the new image.
remediation: If images are mirrored or restricted, add the `startupapicheck` image to the allow-list/mirror before upgrading — the `ctl` image is no longer used.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.image | test("cert-manager")) | .image' | sed 's#/[^/]*$##' | sort -u  # the registry prefix printed is the one that must also carry startupapicheck

title: Known issue in 1.12–1.14: preferredChain may pick the wrong Let's Encrypt chain

detection.reason: `preferredChain` is not in the issuer projection

quote: The problem is that the `preferredChain` feature matches the issuer CN of **any** certificate in the chain.
remediation: If the target is one of these minors and an ACME issuer sets `preferredChain: ISRG Root X1`, either remove the field and renew, or accept the longer cross-signed chain while `DST Root CA X3` is trusted.
verifyCommand: kubectl get issuers,clusterissuers -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.acme.preferredChain // "") != "") | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace // "cluster")/\(.metadata.name) preferredChain=\(.spec.acme.preferredChain)"'  # each row is an issuer the known issue can affect; NO rows = clean
coversNotes: ACME Issuer (Let's Encrypt): wrong certificate chain may be used if `preferredChain` is…

title: CSRs now mark KeyUsage and BasicConstraints critical — strict external CAs may refuse them

detection.reason: whether an external CA honours critical extensions is a property of that CA, not of any collected object

quote: The KeyUsage and BasicConstraints extensions will now be encoded as critical in the CertificateRequest's CSR blob.
remediation: Issue one test Certificate through each Vault and Venafi issuer after the upgrade and confirm the CA accepts the critical extensions.
verifyCommand: kubectl get issuers,clusterissuers -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.vault or .spec.venafi) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace // "cluster")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row signs CSRs the upgrade changes the encoding of
